## Overview

`pipeline()` takes a handful of inputs that vary by year (treatment seeking,
net and spray coverage, the drug in use, resistance and mutation switches,
allele frequencies, importation) and turns them into a **schedule**: one row
per update period, each row holding the values the simulation uses for that
period. The parameters that do not vary are held in a set of classed,
validated **parameter lists**. Both come back with every run inside the
`magenta_sim` object, next to the output, so a result always carries the
inputs that produced it.

This vignette covers the schedule, the parameter lists and their validators,
the result object, and what a seed does and does not reproduce. What the
savers return, and how to save and restart a run, is in the
[Loggers vignette](Loggers.html).


``` r
library(magenta)
quiet <- housekeeping_list_create(quiet = TRUE, cluster = TRUE)
```

---

## The schedule

`build_schedule()` is what `pipeline()` calls; you can call it yourself to see
what a set of inputs will do. One row per period, with the period's first and
last day, the calendar year it falls in, and the yearly inputs for that year.


``` r
sched <- build_schedule(years = 3, update_length = 365, ft = c(0.2, 0.5), itn_cov = 0.3)
sched
## <magenta_schedule> 3 period(s) over 1095 days
##   period day_start day_end year  ft itn_cov irs_cov resistance_flag
## 1      1         1     365    1 0.2     0.3       0           FALSE
## 2      2       366     730    2 0.5     0.3       0           FALSE
## 3      3       731    1095    3 0.5     0.3       0           FALSE
##   mutation_flag drug_choice
## 1         FALSE           0
## 2         FALSE           0
## 3         FALSE           0
```

Three rules are worth knowing.

1. **Last value forward.** A yearly vector shorter than `years` is padded by
   repeating its last value, so `ft = c(0.2, 0.5)` over three years is
   `0.2, 0.5, 0.5`. A vector longer than the run is an error rather than a
   silent truncation.
2. **One row per period.** With `update_save = TRUE` a period is
   `update_length` days; otherwise it is a calendar year. Either way the yearly
   inputs are looked up by the period's `year`, so a period that straddles two
   years takes the values of the year it starts in, and the yearly value of an
   input is simply its value in the first row of that year. Every simulated
   year has to contain the start of a period for that to hold, so an
   `update_length` that would skip a year (one longer than a year, say) is an
   error.
3. **Whole periods only.** The run is `round(years * 365)` days split into
   `round(days / update_length)` periods, which is how the package has always
   counted them: a run of 400 days in 365-day periods is one period of 365
   days.

The schedule is a plain data frame of one value per period: `ft`, `itn_cov`,
`irs_cov`, `resistance_flag`, `mutation_flag` and `drug_choice`, with the
period's days and year. The allele frequencies `plaf` and the two importation
inputs are a vector per year rather than a value, so they do not live in it:
`pipeline()` pads them to a matrix with one row per year by the same rule and
reads the row for the period's year. They come back with the run in
`sim_params(out)` as `plaf`, `spatial_incidence` and `spatial_mosquitoFOI`.


``` r
names(sched)
##  [1] "period"          "day_start"       "day_end"         "year"           
##  [5] "ft"              "itn_cov"         "irs_cov"         "resistance_flag"
##  [9] "mutation_flag"   "drug_choice"
```

`pipeline()` runs one C++ update per row. `ft` is passed to the update
directly; `resistance_flag`, `mutation_flag`, `plaf` and the importation
vectors are switched when a row starts a new year; `itn_cov` and `irs_cov` go
through the mosquito model once for the whole run, taking the value in the
first row of each year, and come back as daily death and feeding rates that
each period slices (see the [Deterministic vignette](Deterministic.html)).
`drug_choice` is filled in as the run goes, so after a run with drug cycling
the schedule records which drug each period used. The schedule a run followed
is returned as `sim_schedule(out)`:


``` r
out <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 1000, years = 3, ft = c(0.2, 0.5), seed = 1L,
                housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 1
## Starting Stochastic Simulation for 3 years
## ||:|2|4|
sim_schedule(out)
## <magenta_schedule> 3 period(s) over 1095 days
##   period day_start day_end year  ft itn_cov irs_cov resistance_flag
## 1      1         1     365    1 0.2       0       0           FALSE
## 2      2       366     730    2 0.5       0       0           FALSE
## 3      3       731    1095    3 0.5       0       0           FALSE
##   mutation_flag drug_choice
## 1         FALSE           0
## 2         FALSE           0
## 3         FALSE           0
```

### Yearly values apply without periodic saving

A run with `update_save = FALSE` still steps year by year, so a treatment
ramp takes effect when it should. Two runs on the same seed, one with
treatment seeking jumping from 0.1 to 0.9 after two years and one holding at
0.1, agree for the first two years and then part:


``` r
ramp <- c(0.1, 0.1, 0.9, 0.9)
with_ramp <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 1000, years = 4, ft = ramp, seed = 1L,
                      update_save = TRUE, update_length = 365,
                      housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 1
## Starting Stochastic Simulation for 4 years
## ||:|2|4|6|
constant <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 1000, years = 4, ft = 0.1, seed = 1L,
                     update_save = TRUE, update_length = 365,
                     housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 1
## Starting Stochastic Simulation for 4 years
## ||:|2|4|6|

prevalence <- function(sim) {
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(sim_schedule(sim))), function(i) {
    l <- sim[[i]]
    if (!is.null(l$Loggers)) l <- l$Loggers
    sum(unlist(l[c("D", "A", "U", "T")]))
  }, numeric(1))
}
rbind(ramp = prevalence(with_ramp), constant = prevalence(constant))
##               [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]
## ramp     0.3740986 0.4308795 0.3443671 0.2496301
## constant 0.3740986 0.4308795 0.4622575 0.4587178
```

The periodic saves are only there to show the years. The same ramp with no
periodic saving returns the final loggers alone, and they are identical to the
final period above, because the periods it ran were the same:


``` r
final_only <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 1000, years = 4, ft = ramp, seed = 1L,
                       housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 1
## Starting Stochastic Simulation for 4 years
## ||:|2|4|6|
sim_schedule(final_only)[, c("period", "year", "ft")]
## <magenta_schedule> 4 period(s)
##   period year  ft
## 1      1    1 0.1
## 2      2    2 0.1
## 3      3    3 0.9
## 4      4    4 0.9
identical(final_only$Loggers, with_ramp[[4]]$Loggers)
## [1] TRUE
```

---

## Parameter lists

Everything that does not vary by year comes in through a parameter list made
by a `*_list_create()` constructor: `model_param_list_create()`,
`drug_list_create()`, `housekeeping_list_create()`, `nmf_list_create()`,
`vector_adaptation_list_create()` and `barcode_list_create()` (the last is
built for you from `pipeline()`'s `num_loci`, `plaf` and related arguments).
Each returns a plain list underneath with a class on top, so it prints
readably and can be validated:


``` r
dl <- drug_list_create()
class(dl)
## [1] "magenta_drug_list"  "magenta_param_list" "list"
dl
## <magenta_drug_list> with 15 fields
##  $ resistance_flag           : logi FALSE
##  $ number_of_resistance_loci : num 2
##  $ resistance_loci           : num 0
##  $ artemisinin_loci          : num 0
##  $ cost_of_resistance        : num [1:4] 1 0.99 0.99 0.98
##  $ absolute_fitness_cost_flag: logi FALSE
##  $ drugs                     :List of 1
##  $ mft_flag                  : logi FALSE
##  $ temporal_cycling          : num -1
##  $ next_temporal_cycle       : num -1
##  $ sequential_cycling        : num -1
##  $ sequential_update         : num 3
##  $ number_of_drugs           : num 1
##  $ drug_choice               : num 0
##  $ partner_drug_ratios       : num 1
```

Each list has a matching exported `validate_*()`. The constructors call it,
and `pipeline()` calls it again on whatever it is given, so a list that has
been edited by hand is checked too. The message names the list and the field:


``` r
dl$partner_drug_ratios <- c(0.5, 0.5)
validate_drug_list(dl)
## Error:
## ! drug_list$partner_drug_ratios must have length 1, not 2
```

What the validators check is the set of fields the C++ simulation reads.
That set is recorded once, as `cpp_contract`: for each list, the fields its
constructor produces and the subset the C++ sources read, and a test checks
both against the sources. It is there for reference when adding a field:


``` r
str(cpp_contract$nmf)
## List of 2
##  $ fields: chr [1:4] "nmf_flag" "mean_nmf_frequency" "nmf_age_brackets" "prob_of_testing_nmf"
##  $ cpp   : chr [1:4] "nmf_flag" "mean_nmf_frequency" "nmf_age_brackets" "prob_of_testing_nmf"
names(cpp_contract)
##  [1] "init"              "update"            "saved_init"       
##  [4] "get"               "finalizer"         "saved_state"      
##  [7] "housekeeping"      "barcode"           "drug"             
## [10] "drug_entry"        "vector_adaptation" "nmf"              
## [13] "spatial"           "eqss"              "core"
```

---

## The `magenta_sim` object

Every run returns what the saver kept, in the shape magenta has always
returned it: the final loggers by default (`out$Loggers`), or one element per
period with `update_save = TRUE` (`out[[i]]`). The object has class
`magenta_sim` and carries three attributes, each with an accessor:

- `sim_params(out)`: the inputs the run was created with, including every
  parameter list,
- `sim_schedule(out)`: the table above, with `drug_choice` filled in,
- `sim_meta(out)`: the call, the seed, the package version, the saver, the
  timings and `rng_state`, the state of R's random number generator when the
  run ended. `attr(out, "meta")` is the same thing, as in earlier versions.

Printing the object gives a short header rather than the whole list;
`unclass(out)` prints the list and its attributes, and `sim_output(out)` is
the bare list with no attributes, which is the thing to compare when checking
that two runs agree.


``` r
out
## <magenta_sim>
##   call:     pipeline(EIR = 5, ft = c(0.2, 0.5), N = 1000, years = 3, seed = 1L,...
##   N: 1000   years: 3   EIR: 5
##   output:   loggers, 1 period(s), final = loggers
##   seed:     1   version: 1.4.0
##   elapsed:  0.4 secs
names(out)
## [1] "Loggers"
names(sim_meta(out))
## [1] "call"        "seed"        "rng_state"   "version"     "saver"      
## [6] "final"       "update_save" "times"       "elapsed"
sim_meta(out)$version
## [1] '1.4.0'
sim_params(out)
## <magenta_params>
##   N: 1000
##   EIR: 5
##   years: 3
##   update_length: NA
##   seed: 1
##   num_loci: 24
##   country: <NULL>
##   admin: <NULL>
##   plaf: <matrix>
##   spatial_incidence: <NULL>
##   spatial_mosquitoFOI: <NULL>
##   core: <magenta_core_params>
##   housekeeping: <magenta_housekeeping_list>
##   drug: <magenta_drug_list>
##   nmf: <magenta_nmf_list>
##   vector_adaptation: <magenta_vector_adaptation_list>
##   barcode: <magenta_barcode_list>
##   spatial: <magenta_spatial_list>
```

`as.data.frame(out)` gives one row per period of the scalar logger values,
and `summary(out)` the headline numbers; both are shown in the
[Loggers vignette](Loggers.html).

---

## Reproducibility

`pipeline()` seeds R's random number generator once, at the start of the run,
and every call into the simulation continues from wherever the generator is.
The seed is recorded in `sim_meta(out)$seed` and in the stored call. The same seed
gives the same run, and a different seed a different one:


``` r
a <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 500, years = 2, seed = 3L, housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 3
## Starting Stochastic Simulation for 2 years
## ||:|2|
b <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 500, years = 2, seed = 3L, housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 3
## Starting Stochastic Simulation for 2 years
## ||:|2|
c <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 500, years = 2, seed = 4L, housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 4
## Starting Stochastic Simulation for 2 years
## ||:|2|
identical(sim_output(a), sim_output(b))
## [1] TRUE
identical(sim_output(a), sim_output(c))
## [1] FALSE
```

A run resumed from a saved state (`saved_state_path =`, see the
[Loggers vignette](Loggers.html#saving-and-restarting)) restores the
generator state the saved run stopped at, so resuming twice from the same
file gives the same result:


``` r
first <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 500, years = 1, seed = 3L,
                  output = save_loggers(final = "full"), housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Seed set to 3
state_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "schedule_state.rds")
sim_save(first, state_file)
again_1 <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 500, years = 1, saved_state_path = state_file,
                    housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Random number generator restored from the saved state
again_2 <- pipeline(EIR = 5, N = 500, years = 1, saved_state_path = state_file,
                    housekeeping_list = quiet)
## magenta v1.4.0
## Random number generator restored from the saved state
identical(sim_output(again_1), sim_output(again_2))
## [1] TRUE
```

What a resumed run does **not** reproduce is an uninterrupted run of the
combined length. The saved state round-trips exactly (every population,
strain, mosquito and parameter list comes back identical), but initialising
from it draws random numbers that the uninterrupted run never drew, so the two
part from the first day of the continuation:


``` r
identical(again_1$Loggers, a$Loggers)
## [1] FALSE
again_1$Loggers$Time == a$Loggers$Time
## [1] TRUE
```

Treat a save-and-resume as its own realisation: reproducible from the file,
not interchangeable with a longer run. Passing `seed` to the resuming call
reseeds instead of restoring, and is reported in the messages.

Because the seeding changed, every seeded run gives different numbers from
magenta 1.3.x; see `NEWS.md`.
